newsitem.title: INDIA: India VSNL sees continued telecom growth.
newsitem.headline: India VSNL sees continued telecom growth.

text.p: India's monopoly state-run international telecommunication provider, Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL) on Friday forecast continued growth in basic telecommunication services after posting strong 1996/97 results.
"The company expects to see continued growth in its principle area of buiness -- basic international telecommunication services," VSNL said in a statement.
VSNL on Friday announced a net profit of 5.03 billion rupees in the year ending March 31, 197 against 4.08 billion in the year-ago period.
"The growth in the traffic volume is encouraging and I expect this trend to continue in the future," B.K. Syngal, VSNL's chairman and managing director said.

The monopoly international telecommunication provider said total volume of telephone traffic transmitted over VSNL's network had increased 20 percent to 1.38 billion paid minutes in 1996/97 from 1.14 billion paid minutes last year.

Rapidly increasing local network and gradual participiation of the private sector in domestic telecommunication services will significantly increase the level of demand for VSNL's international telecommunication services, the firm said.
VSNL completed a $526.6 million Global Depositary Issue in March.
